title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1RE1LD_0LB0LF_1RA1RA_0LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1RE1LD_0LB0LF_1RA1RA_0LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

At the end of each round the tape is a leader 11100, a list of digits of six cells each, a fixed stretch, and a tail of single 1s that grows by one per round. Within an epoch each round changes one or two digits next to a walker that moves left, and the round takes exactly twice as long as the one before plus a constant that depends only on the change. When the walker reaches the front the list is rebuilt longer; the rebuilds are not understood.
verdict: The question is open. No halt in direct simulation to 3.54·1011 steps. The rounds inside an epoch follow an exact law (checked on every round of two epochs, and two rounds predicted before the simulator got there); a halt could only come from a rebuild, whose rule is not known.

claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: The walker law: every round of epochs 2 and 3
claims.text: Write the six-cell units 1 x y 1 0 0 as digits by xy: 00 = 1, 01 = 0, 10 = 2, 11 = 3. In an epoch a walker moves left through the digits. Phase 1 (building 2s): a 0 becomes 1 (c = +16), then that 1 becomes 2 and the walker moves left (c = +4); if the walker finds a 1 that was already there, it becomes 3 (c = +18) and phase 2 starts. Phase 2 (a carry): the digit left of the 3 goes 0 → 1 and the 3 becomes 0 (c = +14), then that 1 becomes 3 and the carry moves left (c = −10); at the front the leader takes the place of the digit (11100 → 10100, c = +14) and the next round is a rebuild. When the phase-1 walker reaches the front (no digit left), the leader also becomes 10100 with the digits unchanged (c = +16, seen once, in epoch 3), and the next round is a rebuild. Each round lasts T′ = 2T + c. From the start of epoch 2 (step 40,509,722, T = 2,926) the law gives all 20 rounds of the epoch to the step (the last ends at 6,201,936,302); from step 12,398,695,221 it gives every round of epoch 3 seen, including 96,327,513,809 and 180,338,374,341, which were predicted before the simulator reached them.
claims.where: python3 py/epoch.py check FILE (FILE from tmrun MACHINE 60000000000 at A R 5000), python3 py/epoch.py ahead

claims.title: Epoch 3 meets the leader
claims.text: In the round ending at step 348,360,095,421 the phase-1 walker, with no digit left, changes the leader 11100 to 10100 and leaves the digits 222222000; the round length is 2T + 16, as py/epoch.py gives it. The round after is a rebuild (step 348,489,525,650), as after the leader change of epoch 2.

claims.title: Epoch 4 starts with a new pattern
claims.text: After the rebuild at 3.48·1011 the list has 14 digits 00000030000010 and the tail N = 2. The first rounds (to step 354,122,694,764) are not in the walker table: the 3 becomes a 2, then the left part runs 0000011, 0000031, 0001001, 0003001, 0010001, 0030001, a carry pattern whose constants are not modelled yet.

claims.title: Where a halt can be (CTL)
claims.text: A closed tape language of windows of up to 6 cells closes, but its abstract configurations still allow F to read a 1 in several contexts, so it does not confine the halt.

claims.title: The rebuilds, and the question
claims.text: Rebuilds at about 2.3·10<sup>4</sup>, 4.05·10<sup>7</sup> 1.2·10<sup>10</sup> and 3.48·10<sup>11</sup> steps turn the tail of single 1s and the fixed stretch into a new, longer list of digits (12, 13, then 14 digits) and a new fixed stretch. Their rule, which decides the next epoch, is not known; nor whether the machine halts.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a two-level counter: a fast counter at the right end of the tape takes twice as long for each round, and each round a walker makes one small change in a list of digits on its left; the length of every round follows exactly from the change. When the walker reaches the front the list is rebuilt longer, in a way nobody has worked out.

facts.text: Predicted to the step by the walker law, in two epochs.
The start of the second epoch, proved in Lean.

sections.heading: Digits, a walker and a doubling clock
html: Stop the machine at the end of each round: the head in state A on the first blank cell right of everything written. The tape then reads

a leader, a list of six-cell units 1 x y 1 0 0, a stretch X that stays fixed for a long time, and a tail of N single 1s. Write each unit as a digit by its middle bits xy: 00 = 1, 01 = 0, 10 = 2, 11 = 3. The tail is the low end of a binary counter: one round is that counter running up to its top, about 2N steps, and the tail is one 1 longer afterwards.
At the end of each round exactly one local change has been made in the digits, at a walker that moves left:

phasechangec
10 → 1 at the walker+16
1that 1 → 2, walker one digit left+4
1 → 2an old 1 → 3+18
20 3 → 1 0+14
2that 1 → 3, walker one digit left−10

and the new round lasts exactly T′ = 2T + c, with T the length of the round before. In the second epoch, which starts at step 40,509,722 with the digits 0000100000, the walker turns the last five 0s into 2s, meets the old 1, and carries a 3 to the front: 20 rounds, ending at step 6,201,936,302, every one of them to the step. The third epoch, from step 12.4·109, follows the same law.

rules.text: phase 1, a 0 at the walker becomes 1: T′ = 2T + 16 (py/epoch.py)
phase 1, that 1 becomes 2 and the walker moves left: T′ = 2T + 4
an old 1 becomes 3, phase 2 starts: T′ = 2T + 18
phase 2, the carry moves left: T′ = 2T − 10

stepper.note: Starts at the start of epoch 2 (step 40,509,722, proved in Lean by epoch2_start). Press, in order: (0 → 1, 1 → 2) five times, then 1 → 3 (phase 2), then (0 3 → 1 0, 1 → 3) four times, then 0 3 → 1 0 once more at the leader: the step reads 6,201,936,302, where the machine starts its rebuild. The stepper does arithmetic only; the order of the changes comes from the digits.

sections.heading: Rebuilds
html: After the leader changes (at the end of the carry, or when the phase-1 walker reaches it), the next round is different: the tail of single 1s and the fixed stretch X are turned into a new, longer list of digits and a new X, and the tail starts again short. This happened at about 2.3·104, 4.05·107 1.2·1010 and 3.48·1011 steps; the lists after them have 4, 12, 13 and 14 digits. In the round ending at step 348,360,095,421 the phase-1 walker, with no digit left, changes the leader 11100 to 10100 and leaves the digits 222222000; the round length is 2T + 16, as py/epoch.py gives it. The round after is a rebuild (step 348,489,525,650), as after the leader change of epoch 2.

The rule of a rebuild is not known, so the run can be followed by arithmetic only to the end of an epoch. A halt (F reading a 1) can come only from a rebuild: inside an epoch the rounds repeat the same five local changes.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.097).
After 109 steps the tape spans 182 cells (24 left of the start, 155 right), with a density of 1s of 0.571.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

family: two-level counter: a fast binary counter at the right end, one walker step per round in a list of 6-cell digits, rebuilds
summary: A two-level counter: each round the fast counter at the right end doubles its time and a walker makes one local change in a list of 6-cell digits, with round length T' = 2T + c(change) exactly; the law predicts every round of two epochs (40 rounds, up to 1.8e11 steps); the rebuilds between epochs are not modelled; open.
